payload.title: Ship the agents command for Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context
When a person uses Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI in WSL and on Windows, they want one command that shows and updates every agent and the Codex app-server daemon, so they stop running each updater by hand every day. Orchestrator decision on dev-j6oqo (2026-11-21 10:43 UTC): ship it in terminal, reuse the --agents installer code, no second set of installer URLs, no user names or machine paths, refuse npm or brew installs by name with the correct command, uninstall only with a test, agents.cmd falls back to powershell.exe, keep the CODEX_INSTALL_DAEMON_ONLY=1 Windows daemon fallback and warn before a daemon update. Source: the <redacted:machine-username>-f2 scripts (agents, agents.ps1, agents.cmd).

## Confirmation Plan
Run the agents tests with faked version lookups, shellcheck on the rendered script, quality-gates on the commit, and an e2e-install run by workflow_dispatch on the pushed branch.

When agents status runs, it shall print the installed and latest version and a state of ok, update, missing or unknown for claude, codex, the codex daemon and copilot.
When agents update runs, it shall run only the updaters of agents whose state is not ok, unless --force is given.
When an agent binary resolves into an npm or brew install, agents shall refuse to update it by name and print the correct npm or brew command.

When agents uninstall runs with confirmation, it shall remove the agent binaries and keep the configuration folders, proven by a test on a fake home.
When agents.cmd runs without pwsh, it shall run agents.ps1 with powershell.exe.

payload.description:
## Context
When the claim-burst test test_a_live_sharer_finishes_after_takeover_without_lost_or_duplicate_events fails on a loaded CI runner, I want the failure to name whether the takeover push timed out or was rejected, so I can fix the race at its cause instead of guessing.

## Evidence
Seen: quality-gates run 44789777530 shard 7/12 (2026-11-20 18:08 UTC): joined claim exit 4, 'the vault refused the share 1 times; 2 events stay queued'; leader exit 0.
Not reproduced: 50 loops of tests/test_kit_vault_claim_burst.py, taskset -c 16-31, pytest -n 4, 250 test runs, all passed (2026-11-21 10:46-11:04 UTC).
Code facts: vault_share.share reports any GitRunnerError from the push as 'refused'; GitTimeoutError is a GitRunnerError (git_runner.py:53), so a push timeout reads as a refusal.
Hypothesis, not proven: with deadline=2 the join waits for a stall of min(STALL, joined_at/2), about 0.95 s of the 1.9 s budget, before the unlocked takeover; the takeover then runs fetch, seven git build steps and a hooked push in the rest, and a loaded runner can pass that deadline.
payload.title: Name the cause when a takeover share push fails in the live sharer claim burst test
